question: I need my Canadian credit history before renting. Which two main credit bureaus provide free reports, and will checking my own report lower my credit score?
generated_answer:
In Canada, there are two main credit bureaus that provide free credit reports: Equifax and TransUnion. You can request a free credit report from each of them once a year.

To get your free credit report, you can:

* Contact Equifax Canada at 1-800-465-7166 or visit their website at [www.equifax.ca](http://www.equifax.ca)
* Contact TransUnion Canada at 1-800-663-9980 or visit their website at [www.transunion.ca](http://www.transunion.ca)

Checking your own credit report will not lower your credit score. This is known as a "soft inquiry," and it's considered a self-initiated request for your own information. Soft inquiries do not affect your credit score.

On the other hand, when a lender or creditor checks your credit report, it's considered a "hard inquiry," which can temporarily lower your credit score. But don't worry, checking your own report is a good idea to ensure the information is accurate and up-to-date, especially before renting or applying for credit.
